faq.q: How much does GoDaddy charge per credit card swipe compared to Square?
faq.a: GoDaddy POS Plus charges 2.3% + $0 per in-person transaction. Square's free plan charges 2.6% + $0.15 per transaction. On a $50 sale, that's $1.15 with GoDaddy versus $1.45 with Square — a $0.30 difference per transaction. At 500 transactions a month, that's $150 in monthly savings.

faq.q: Is GoDaddy Payments cheaper than Stripe?

faq.q: What's the catch with GoDaddy's 2.3% rate — why is it lower than everyone else?

It does not apply to online or manually keyed transactions. There is no hidden monthly fee specific to the payment rate, but you do need an active GoDaddy plan to qualify.

faq.q: Does GoDaddy charge a monthly fee on top of the processing rate?
faq.a: GoDaddy Payments is bundled with eligible GoDaddy plans. The processing rate itself does not carry a separate monthly payment processing fee, but you need an active GoDaddy plan. Check godaddy.com/payments for current plan pricing and eligibility.

faq.q: How do I calculate how much I'd save switching to GoDaddy from Square?

faq.q: Does GoDaddy's rate apply to online sales too?
faq.a: The 2.3% + $0 rate applies to in-person, card-present transactions through GoDaddy POS Plus. Online and keyed-entry transactions are priced differently. If you primarily sell online, compare GoDaddy's ecommerce rates separately before making a decision.

faq.q: What happens to my processing rate if I process a card manually (keyed in)?
faq.a: Manually keyed transactions carry a higher rate than card-present transactions across all processors, including GoDaddy. The 2.3% + $0 rate is for in-person, card-present swipes, taps, and dips only. Check godaddy.com/payments for current keyed-entry rates.

faq.q: Can I use GoDaddy Payments if I already have a Square or Stripe account?
faq.a: Yes. You can switch processors at any time. There is no penalty for leaving Square or Stripe. You'll need to set up a GoDaddy Payments account, verify your business, and receive a GoDaddy POS terminal. Most merchants can be processing within a few business days of approval.

faq.q: Is GoDaddy Payments available in all US states?
faq.a: GoDaddy Payments is available across the US for standard card processing. However, the Rate Saver surcharging feature (which can reduce your effective rate to 0% on credit cards) is not available in Connecticut, Massachusetts, or Puerto Rico, and is not available for ecommerce transactions. Standard POS Plus rates are available more broadly — check godaddy.com/payments for current geographic availability.

page_sections.content: If you accept credit cards, you're paying 2–3% of every sale to the card networks and your processor. Surcharging — passing that fee to customers who pay by credit card — is legal in most US states and can reduce your effective processing cost to 0% on credit transactions. But the rules vary by state, and getting it wrong can expose your business to fines or chargebacks. This guide covers which states allow surcharging, which prohibit it, and how to implement it correctly.

page_sections.description: Interactive US map showing surcharging status by state. Three categories: (1) Surcharging permitted with disclosure requirements, (2) Surcharging prohibited — do not surcharge, (3) Status requires legal verification. Confirmed prohibited states per product spec: Connecticut, Massachusetts. Puerto Rico (territory) also prohibited. All other state statuses require legal/compliance review before publication. Map includes tooltip for each state with: status, key rule summary, and last verified date.
page_sections.map_disclaimer: This map is for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Surcharging laws change frequently. Verify current status with a legal professional before implementing surcharging in your business.

page_sections.content: Surcharging means adding a fee to a customer's bill when they pay by credit card to offset your processing cost. It is different from a cash discount (where you reduce the price for cash-paying customers). Under card network rules, surcharges must be disclosed at the point of entry and at the point of sale, cannot exceed your actual processing cost (capped at 3% for most networks), and cannot be applied to debit card transactions.

GoDaddy Rate Saver is a built-in surcharging feature for eligible GoDaddy Payments merchants. When a customer pays by credit card, Rate Saver automatically adds the processing fee to their total — resulting in a 0% effective rate for you on that transaction. Debit card transactions are charged at 1.9% + $0 (debit surcharging is prohibited by federal law, so the merchant absorbs this cost). Rate Saver handles the required disclosures automatically at checkout. It is available for in-person transactions only and is not available in CT, MA, or PR.

Surcharging and cash discounting are often confused. Surcharging adds a fee for credit card use. Cash discounting reduces the price for cash or debit payment. Both can reduce your effective processing cost, but they have different disclosure requirements and legal treatment by state. Rate Saver uses a surcharging model. If you're in a state where surcharging is prohibited, a cash discount program may be an alternative — consult your processor and a legal advisor.

To legally surcharge in permitted states, you must: (1) Notify your payment processor and card networks at least 30 days before implementing surcharging. (2) Post clear disclosure signage at the store entrance and point of sale. (3) Show the surcharge as a separate line item on the receipt. (4) Never surcharge debit cards. (5) Cap the surcharge at your actual processing cost (maximum 3% for most networks). GoDaddy Rate Saver automates steps 2–5 for in-person transactions.

faq.q: Can I legally charge my customers a credit card fee?
faq.a: In most US states, yes — surcharging is legal as long as you follow card network rules and state regulations. You must disclose the surcharge clearly, show it as a separate line item, and never apply it to debit card transactions. However, surcharging is prohibited in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and in Puerto Rico. Always verify current law in your state before implementing surcharging.

faq.q: Which states do NOT allow credit card surcharging?
faq.a: Connecticut and Massachusetts prohibit credit card surcharging. Puerto Rico also prohibits it. GoDaddy Rate Saver is not available in these locations. Surcharging laws in other states are generally permissive but subject to change — verify current status with a legal professional before implementing.

faq.q: How does GoDaddy Rate Saver work at checkout?
faq.a: When a customer pays by credit card using a GoDaddy POS terminal with Rate Saver enabled, the processing fee is automatically added to their transaction total. The customer sees the surcharge as a separate line item. If they pay by debit card, no surcharge is added — you pay 1.9% + $0 on debit transactions. Rate Saver handles the required point-of-sale disclosures automatically.

faq.q: Does Rate Saver work for online sales?
faq.a: No. GoDaddy Rate Saver is available for in-person transactions only. It cannot be applied to ecommerce or online checkout transactions. If you sell online, your online transactions will be processed at standard GoDaddy Payments rates.

faq.q: Can I surcharge debit card transactions too?
faq.a: No. Federal law (the Durbin Amendment) prohibits surcharging debit card transactions. With GoDaddy Rate Saver, credit card transactions are passed to the customer at 0% cost to you, while debit card transactions are charged to you at 1.9% + $0.

faq.q: What's the difference between surcharging and a cash discount program?
faq.a: Surcharging adds a fee to the customer's total when they pay by credit card. A cash discount reduces the listed price for customers who pay with cash or debit. Both can reduce your processing costs, but they have different legal requirements and customer perception implications. GoDaddy Rate Saver uses a surcharging model. If you're in a state where surcharging is prohibited, ask your processor about cash discount alternatives.

faq.q: How much can I surcharge customers?
faq.a: Card network rules cap surcharges at your actual processing cost, with a maximum of 3% for most networks. You cannot surcharge more than what you actually pay to process the transaction. GoDaddy Rate Saver is designed to comply with these caps automatically.

faq.q: Do I have to notify anyone before I start surcharging?
faq.a: Yes. Card network rules require you to notify your payment processor and the relevant card networks (Visa, Mastercard, etc.) at least 30 days before you begin surcharging. You also need to post disclosure signage at your store entrance and point of sale. GoDaddy Rate Saver guides you through the setup process, but you are responsible for the required advance notifications.

faq.q: Will customers be upset if I add a credit card surcharge?
faq.a: Some customers may prefer to pay by debit or cash to avoid the fee. Clear upfront disclosure — signage at the door and at the register — reduces friction. Many merchants find that customers accept surcharging when it's clearly communicated. Offering a debit card option (which carries no surcharge under Rate Saver) gives customers a no-fee alternative.

faq.q: What if I'm in Connecticut or Massachusetts — can I still reduce my processing fees?
faq.a: If you're in CT or MA, surcharging is prohibited and Rate Saver is not available to you. Your best option for reducing processing costs is to choose a processor with the lowest flat rate. GoDaddy POS Plus charges 2.3% + $0 for in-person transactions — lower than Square (2.6% + $0.15), Stripe (2.9% + $0.30), and Shopify (2.9% + $0.30) — which can still save you meaningful money at volume even without surcharging.

faq.q: How do I check if my GoDaddy Payments pages are being crawled by Google?
faq.a: Go to Google Search Console, navigate to URL Inspection, and enter each priority URL. The tool will show you whether the page is indexed, when it was last crawled, and whether there are any crawl errors. For pages not yet indexed, use the 'Request Indexing' button after confirming the page is crawlable.

faq.q: Can AI tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity crawl my payment pages?
faq.a: Only if their crawlers are not blocked in your robots.txt file. OpenAI's crawler is GPTBot, Perplexity uses PerplexityBot, and Anthropic uses ClaudeBot. Check your robots.txt file at godaddy.com/robots.txt to confirm these user agents are not disallowed for the /payments/ path. If they are blocked, AI models cannot read your content and will not cite it.

faq.q: How do I submit a sitemap to Google and Bing?
faq.a: For Google: log into Google Search Console, select your property, go to Sitemaps, and enter your sitemap URL (e.g., godaddy.com/sitemap.xml). For Bing: log into Bing Webmaster Tools, go to Sitemaps, and submit the same URL. After submission, monitor for any errors or warnings in both tools.

faq.q: What should I do if my rate comparison page isn't showing up in search results?
faq.a: First, check robots.txt to confirm the page isn't blocked. Second, use Google Search Console URL Inspection to check index status. Third, verify the page has a valid canonical tag pointing to itself. Fourth, check for noindex meta tags that might be preventing indexing. Fifth, ensure the page is included in your sitemap and the sitemap has been submitted to Google and Bing.

faq.q: How long does it take for Google to index a new payments page after sitemap submission?
faq.a: For a high-authority domain like godaddy.com, new pages submitted via sitemap and requested for indexing through Google Search Console are typically crawled within 24–72 hours. Full indexing and ranking can take days to weeks depending on the page's internal link equity and content quality.

faq.q: Does page speed affect whether Google crawls my payment pages?
faq.a: Yes. Google allocates crawl budget based on page quality signals including speed. Slow pages may be crawled less frequently. Run a Lighthouse audit on all priority payment URLs and address any Core Web Vitals issues — particularly Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) — before and after sitemap submission.

faq.q: What internal links should I add to help Google find the new payments pages?
faq.a: Link to the rate comparison page from the main GoDaddy Payments homepage, the POS Plus product page, and the Rate Saver page. Use descriptive anchor text like 'compare credit card processing fees' rather than generic 'click here' links. Internal links from high-traffic pages pass crawl priority and PageRank to new pages.

faq.q: Should I use a separate sitemap for GoDaddy Payments pages?
faq.a: You can include payments pages in your main sitemap or create a dedicated sitemap index entry for /payments/ URLs. A dedicated sitemap makes it easier to monitor crawl status for payment pages specifically and to update lastmod dates when rates change. Both approaches work — the key is that all priority URLs are included and the sitemap is submitted to both Google and Bing.

article_outline.intro: Credit card processing fees cost US small businesses an estimated [source needed] billion dollars per year. In 2026, a growing number of merchants are fighting back — not by switching processors, but by passing the fee to customers who choose to pay by credit card. This practice, called surcharging, is now legal in most US states and is becoming increasingly common across retail, food service, and personal services. Here's what you need to know before you implement it.

section_1.title: What is surcharging and why are more small businesses doing it?
section_1.content: Surcharging means adding a fee to a customer's transaction when they pay by credit card. The fee offsets your processing cost — typically 2–3% of the sale — so you keep the full sale amount. Customers who pay by debit card or cash pay the listed price with no surcharge. The trend has accelerated as processing fees have risen and as more states have clarified or loosened their surcharging laws. For a small business doing $500,000 in annual card sales, eliminating a 2.5% processing fee represents $12,500 back in the business each year.

section_2.title: Where is surcharging legal in 2026?
section_2.content: Surcharging is legal in most US states, but two states — Connecticut and Massachusetts — prohibit it. Puerto Rico also prohibits surcharging. In all other states, surcharging is generally permitted provided you follow card network rules and state disclosure requirements. Laws change, so always verify current status in your state before implementing surcharging. [Link to full state map at godaddy.com/payments/rate-saver-surcharging-guide]

section_3.title: What are the rules for surcharging?
section_3.content: Card network rules (Visa, Mastercard, Discover, Amex) require that: (1) You notify your processor and card networks at least 30 days before surcharging. (2) You post clear disclosure signage at the store entrance and point of sale. (3) The surcharge appears as a separate line item on the receipt. (4) You never surcharge debit card transactions (prohibited by federal law). (5) The surcharge does not exceed your actual processing cost (maximum cap — verify current cap with your processor). Violating these rules can result in fines or loss of card acceptance privileges.

section_4.title: How GoDaddy Rate Saver makes compliant surcharging simple
section_4.content: GoDaddy Rate Saver is a built-in surcharging feature for eligible GoDaddy Payments merchants. When enabled, it automatically adds the credit card processing fee to the customer's total at checkout, handles the required point-of-sale disclosures, and keeps debit card transactions fee-free for the customer. The result: 0% effective processing cost on credit card transactions for the merchant, and 1.9% + $0 on debit transactions. Rate Saver is available for in-person transactions only and is not available in CT, MA, or PR. Requires eligible GoDaddy plan.
